title: Today the angels sing and Adam is renewed

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 9, col. D, to p. 10, col. A (PDF pp. 33-34)

source_text: Hodie ab Angelicis choris laudes divinae celebrantur, et lumen Christi adventus fidelibus illucescit. Hodie laetum nobis ver, Christus sol iustitiae affulsit, ac claro nos lumine collustravit, fideliumque mentes illuminavit. Hodie renovatur Adam, et choros cum Angelis agit, in caelum sublatus. Hodie totus terrarum orbis, gaudio ob adventum Spiritus Sancti in homines, plenus est. Hodie divina gratia, spes invisibilium effulget, et miracula quae mentem atque intelligentiam superant, mysteriumque quod ab aeterno occultatum fuit, palam nobis facit.
pass_a_gloss: Today (hodie) by angelic choirs (chorus angelicus) divine praises (laudes divinae) are celebrated (celebrantur), and the light (lumen) of Christ's coming (adventus) dawns (illucescit) for the faithful (fideles). Today a glad spring (ver laetum) for us, Christ the sun of justice (sol iustitiae), has shone forth (affulsit), and has lit us all round (collustravit) with clear light, and has illuminated (illuminavit) the minds (mentes) of the faithful. Today Adam is renewed (renovatur), and leads/joins dances (choros agit) with the angels, raised (sublatus) into heaven. Today the whole circle of lands (totus terrarum orbis) is full (plenus) of joy (gaudium) on account of the coming (adventus) of the Holy Spirit (Spiritus Sanctus) into/upon men (in homines). Today divine grace (divina gratia), hope of invisible things (spes invisibilium), shines out (effulget), and the miracles (miracula) which surpass (superant) mind (mens) and understanding (intelligentia), and the mystery (mysterium) which was hidden (occultatum) from eternity (ab aeterno), [divine grace] makes plain (palam facit) to us.

choices.issue: He makes plain to us the mystery...
choices.choice: Section 1 English currently opens 'He makes plain to us the mystery...', which gives the verb the wrong subject; if the parent merges this row into section 1, section 1's opening should become something like 'together with the mystery hidden from eternity, it makes plain to us.' 'sol iustitiae' = Malachi 4:2 in English Bibles (Malachi 3:20 in the Hebrew/Vulgate numbering), cited.
'spes invisibilium' may recall Romans 8:24-25 or Hebrews 11:1; uncertain, not cited.
'choros agit' rendered 'dances in the choirs' (chorus = choral dance).

pass_b_english: Today the choirs of angels sing divine praises, and the light of Christ's coming dawns on the faithful. Today is a glad spring for us: Christ, the Sun of Righteousness (Malachi 4:2), has shone forth, has lit us all around with clear light, and has enlightened the minds of the faithful. Today Adam is made new, and, lifted up into heaven, he dances in the choirs with the angels. Today the whole world is full of joy at the coming of the Holy Spirit upon humankind. Today divine grace, the hope of things unseen, shines out, and makes plain to us the wonders that surpass mind and understanding and the mystery that was hidden from eternity.
notes: Grammar of the last sentence: divina gratia is the subject of both effulget and facit; miracula and mysterium are both objects of palam facit. So the full sense is: Today divine grace, the hope of things unseen, shines out and makes plain to us the wonders that surpass mind and understanding, and the mystery hidden from eternity.
source_notes: Vossius print (sources/gregory_thaumaturgus_opera_omnia.pdf, PDF page 33 = printed p. 9, Latin column D, under the heading 'In Annunciationem sanctissimae Dei genitricis virginis Mariae, sermo I'); last two words 'mentem ... superant' run on to PDF p. 34 = printed p. 10, col. A. This is the true opening of Sermo I. Its last sentence ends at '... superant, mysteriumque quod ab aeterno occultatum fuit, palam nobis facit' (printed p. 10, col. A, lowercase 'mysteriumque' as printed); that clause was moved here from the start of section 1 so the sentence is not split. Margin beside 'renovatur' carries a variant ('al. ...'), too small to read with confidence. Long s, u/v, ligatures and ampersands normalised; text otherwise as printed.

changes: 'laetum nobis ver' made a predicate ('Today is a glad spring for us'); Christ, not the spring, is the subject of affulsit, as the print's punctuation shows

2026-10-23 assembly: the clause 'mysteriumque quod ab aeterno occultatum fuit, palam nobis facit' moved from the start of section 1 to the end of this row (print p. 10, col. A), and the English sentence completed with divine grace as subject ('and makes plain to us ... the mystery that was hidden from eternity').
